objective: Bound what the release and governance gates read, so a large or hostile input is refused with its path and limit instead of being loaded whole or truncated.
decision_supported: Should each gate keep its own unbounded read_text/json.loads, or share one bounded reader that refuses oversize input?
acceptance: A JSON document over the limit is refused with its path and the limit.
A text document over the limit is refused the same way.
A document at the limit is still accepted.
An oversize document is never truncated and returned.
Duplicate keys and invalid UTF-8 are still refused.
No gate keeps an unbounded read_text, and every gate uses the shared reader.
The gates still report INCOMPLETE rather than raising when an input is unreadable.
commands: python3 -m pytest tests/unit/test_task_packet.py tests/unit/test_phase_gates.py tests/unit/test_readiness_report.py tests/unit/test_ready_gate.py tests/unit/test_evaluation_tools.py -q
evidence: Before the change five gates called Path.read_text and json.loads directly, so an input of any size was loaded whole.
After the change an 8388716-byte JSON document is refused at the 8388608-byte limit and a 4194404-byte Markdown document at the 4194304-byte limit, each naming the path.
A test enumerates the five gates and asserts none of them contains an unbounded read_text and each imports the shared reader.
239 tests across the gate suites pass, including the ones asserting an unreadable input yields INCOMPLETE.
stop_conditions: A legitimate input exceeds 8 MiB of JSON or 4 MiB of text; the limits are two constants in _jsonio and the refusal names them.
risks_and_fallbacks: The gates now raise JsonInputError where they previously raised OSError or JSONDecodeError; each gate's except clause was widened so the INCOMPLETE outcome is unchanged.
The duplicate-key message is now shared, so one Task Packet test that matched the old wording was updated to the shared phrase.
